title: GPU Accelerated Sparse Cholesky Factorization
problem: Sparse Cholesky factorization is compute intensive and time-consuming on CPU alone. The task is to accelerate the direct solution of sparse symmetric positive definite linear systems by reducing factorization time.
motivation: Solving sparse linear systems is a critical computational kernel in large-scale scientific and engineering modeling and simulation.
method: Cholesky factorization breaks into dense matrix blocks and sparse structure management. The method uses a right-looking approach (processing the matrix from right to left), which naturally exposes dense sub-matrices that need intensive calculations. The GPU accelerates these dense blocks since it excels at large repetitive matrix math, while the CPU coordinates which blocks to compute and when, based on the sparse structure.
key_novelty: Sparse Cholesky factorization naturally contains dense sub-blocks that the GPU can handle much faster than the CPU, so the method offloads those blocks while keeping sparse coordination on the CPU.
contributions: GPU-accelerated sparse Cholesky factorization using right-looking approach
Techniques for identifying and offloading dense matrix operations to GPU
